Assessment
- Macro tone from the FOMC statement: Hawkish. Growth described as modest; labor market strong; inflation “elevated”; policy set to continue tightening via higher rates and balance sheet reduction, with high vigilance on inflation risks.
- SLOOS overlay (July 2022): Banks broadly tightened lending standards and terms across C&I (all firm sizes), CRE, and most residential mortgage categories, and for consumer credit (e.g., credit cards, subprime auto). Banks also increased loan costs and collateralization, frequently citing a deteriorating economic outlook and liquidity concerns. Demand was mixed—stronger for C&I and HELOCs, weaker in some CRE categories.
- Implication: The SLOOS points to a clear tightening in credit supply that amplifies the FOMC’s restrictive stance, raising downside growth risks beyond a purely macro read. While demand remains resilient in some segments, the breadth of tightening and higher borrowing costs point to more negative sentiment overall, albeit tempered by still-resilient banking fundamentals noted in contemporaneous Fed assessments.

Overall stance: Cautious/hawkish and more negative given SLOOS-confirmed credit tightening and elevated downside risks.
